extra_vocab.note: 多益常見於公告、規定與客服信件，表示「馬上、不得延遲」。也常放在介系詞前面，說明「緊接在…之後」，如 immediately after、immediately upon arrival。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: immediately 可放在 after、upon、following 前面，加強「緊接著」：immediately after the meeting、immediately upon arrival（upon 後面接名詞或 V-ing）。

example.en: Please call me immediately after the meeting ends.
example.zh: 會議一結束請立刻打給我。

example.en: Guests must sign in immediately upon arrival at the office.
example.zh: 訪客一抵達辦公室就必須簽到。

example.en: We should respond immediately to every serious customer complaint.
example.zh: 我們應該立即回應每一件嚴重的客訴。

examples.en: Please stop using the machine immediately if it makes noise.
examples.zh: 如果機器發出噪音，請立刻停止使用。

examples.en: I will send you the updated file immediately, Ms. Lee.
examples.zh: 李小姐，我會立刻把更新的檔案寄給您。

examples.en: He left the office immediately to meet the client.
examples.zh: 他立刻離開辦公室去見客戶。

confusable.diff: imminent 是形容詞，表示「即將發生的」；immediately 是副詞，表示「馬上、沒有延遲」。
confusable.usage: imminent 修飾事情，如 an imminent decision；immediately 修飾動作，如 reply immediately。

example.en: A decision about the new contract is imminent.
example.zh: 關於新合約的決定即將出爐。

similar.diff: 更口語，常用在日常對話與電子郵件。

example.en: Please reply to this customer email right away.
example.zh: 請馬上回覆這封客戶郵件。

similar.diff: 語氣較強，常用在命令或緊急通知。

example.en: All staff must leave the building at once.
example.zh: 所有員工必須立刻離開大樓。

derived.link: immediate 是詞幹；immediate + -ly 變成副詞，像 quick → quickly。

extra_vocab.en: to officially order that something must be done
extra_vocab.note: 多益常見於法規、公司政策與新聞，指政府或公司「強制要求」，常用被動 be mandated by law；當名詞則指「官方命令」或「授權」。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: mandate that 後面的子句動詞用原形（或 should + 原形）：The law mandates that all workers wear helmets。動詞常用被動：be mandated by law。

example.en: The government mandates safety checks for all new equipment.
example.zh: 政府強制規定所有新設備都要做安全檢查。

example.en: The company mandated remote work during the storm.
example.zh: 公司在暴風雨期間強制規定遠距工作。

example.en: The city is mandating recycling for all offices.
example.zh: 市政府正強制要求所有辦公室做資源回收。

example.en: Safety training is mandated by law in this industry.
example.zh: 這個產業的安全訓練是法律強制規定的。

example.en: The contract mandates that payment be made within thirty days.
example.zh: 合約規定款項必須在三十天內付清。

example.en: The new government mandate affects every food business.
example.zh: 這項新的政府規定影響所有食品業者。

examples.en: All employees are mandated to attend the safety briefing.
examples.zh: 所有員工都被規定必須參加安全說明會。

examples.en: The CEO received a clear mandate to cut costs.
examples.zh: 執行長獲得明確的授權去削減成本。

examples.en: Federal rules mandate regular fire drills in office buildings.
examples.zh: 聯邦規定要求辦公大樓定期舉行消防演習。

confusable.diff: demand 是「要求、需求」，不一定有官方效力；mandate 是官方或法律上的強制規定。

example.en: Customer demand for our product grew rapidly this year.
example.zh: 今年顧客對我們產品的需求快速成長。

similar.diff: 更一般、更常用；mandate 語氣更正式，強調官方強制。

example.en: The company requires all visitors to sign in at the desk.
example.zh: 公司要求所有訪客在櫃檯簽到。

derived.link: mandate 去掉 e + -ory，形容詞，意思是被強制規定的。

example.en: The company will mandate training for all new employees.
example.zh: 公司將強制規定所有新進員工參加訓練。

example.en: The union has a mandate to negotiate on behalf of workers.
example.zh: 工會獲得授權代表工人進行協商。

extra_vocab.zh: 覺得受到不公平的對待
extra_vocab.en: to feel that you were treated in an unfair way
extra_vocab.note: 偏英式口語，常見於對話與聽力，描述自己在工作或分配上吃虧、覺得不公平。
extra_vocab.pattern: feel / be + hard done by (+ when / because 子句)
extra_vocab.grammar_note: hard done by 是固定的形容詞片語（源自 be done by），後面不再接受詞；前面搭配 feel 或 be，後面要說原因時用 when 或 because 引導子句。

examples.en: She felt hard done by when the bonus went to someone else.
examples.zh: 當獎金給了別人時，她覺得受到不公平的對待。

examples.en: Many staff feel hard done by after the pay cut.
examples.zh: 減薪之後，許多員工覺得自己被虧待了。

examples.en: Do not feel hard done by; everyone had to work overtime.
examples.zh: 別覺得被不公平對待，每個人都得加班。

similar.diff: 意思相同，說法較直白、中性，英美都通用。

example.en: He feels unfairly treated because of the new schedule.
example.zh: 他覺得新的班表對他不公平。

similar.diff: 指實際上拿到不公平的待遇，不只是「感覺」；feel hard done by 強調主觀感受。

example.en: Part-time workers often get a raw deal on pay.
example.zh: 兼職人員在薪資上常常吃虧。

confusable.diff: be hard on 是「對…嚴苛」，主詞是做出嚴苛行為的人；feel hard done by 的主詞是被不公平對待的人。

example.en: The manager was hard on the new staff.
example.zh: 經理對新進員工很嚴格。

extra_vocab.en: a change that happens because of something
extra_vocab.note: 多益最常見的是名詞：have an effect on（對…有影響）、side effect（副作用），以及法規「生效」的 take effect、go into effect。要區分：effect 是名詞，effective 是形容詞（有效的），affect 是動詞（影響）。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: 規定「生效」的主詞是規定本身：The rule takes effect / goes into effect / comes into effect（effect 前不加 a、the）；由人或機構「實施」規定，用 put the rule into effect。

example.en: Some medicines have side effects, so please read the label.
example.zh: 有些藥有副作用，所以請閱讀標籤。

example.en: The new tax rules will take effect on the first of January.
example.zh: 新的稅務規定將在一月一日生效。

collocations.phrase: come into effect / go into effect

example.en: The new computer sign-in system will go into effect tomorrow.
example.zh: 新的電腦登入系統明天開始生效。

example.en: The weather can have an effect on our delivery times.
example.zh: 天氣可能對我們的送貨時間有影響。

example.en: A secondary effect of the new schedule is lower overtime cost.
example.zh: 新班表的次要影響是加班費降低。

example.en: The ban on overtime work is still in effect this month.
example.zh: 加班禁令這個月仍然有效。

examples.en: We are studying the long-term effects of remote work.
examples.zh: 我們正在研究遠距工作的長期影響。

examples.en: The price cut had a positive effect on our monthly sales.
examples.zh: 降價對我們的月銷售有正面的影響。

examples.en: The special effects in the product video impressed the clients.
examples.zh: 產品影片裡的特效讓客戶印象深刻。

confusable.diff: affect 是動詞「影響」，effect 多半是名詞「影響、效果」。
confusable.usage: 動詞用 affect + 受詞（affect sales）；名詞用 have an effect on（have an effect on sales）。

example.en: The delay will affect our delivery schedule this week.
example.zh: 這次延誤會影響我們本週的出貨時程。

confusable.diff: effective 是形容詞「有效的」，effect 是名詞，不能互換。
confusable.usage: effective 修飾名詞或接在 be 後面（an effective plan）；effective + 日期 表示「自…起生效」。

example.en: The new advertising plan was very effective in raising sales.
example.zh: 新的廣告計畫在提升銷售上非常有效。

similar.diff: 人或機構「實施」規定，後面接規定當受詞；take effect 則是規定自己「生效」。

example.en: The company will put the new policy into effect on Monday.
example.zh: 公司將在星期一實施新政策。

similar.diff: apply to 表示規定「適用於」某些人或情況，不是「生效」的意思。

example.en: This rule applies to all staff in the Taipei office.
example.zh: 這項規定適用於台北辦公室的所有員工。

example.en: The result of the test was better than we expected.
example.zh: 測試的結果比我們預期的好。

example.en: The new law will have a big impact on small shops.
example.zh: 新法律將對小店造成很大的衝擊。

derived.link: effect + -ive，形容詞「有效果的」，像 active、creative。
effective + -ly，形容詞變副詞，像 quick → quickly。
effective + -ness，把「有效」變成名詞，像 kind → kindness。
in- + effective，in- 表示「不」，像 incorrect。

example.en: The training had a clear effect on the team's results.
example.zh: 這次訓練對團隊的成績有明顯的影響。

senses.en: the time when a rule or law starts to be used
senses.distinguish: 出現在 take effect、go into effect、in effect 等片語，主詞是法規、制度或政策時，指「生效、有效」。

example.en: The new rule has been in effect since the beginning of the month.
example.zh: 這項新規定從月初起就已經生效了。

extra_vocab.en: in a very big and sudden way
extra_vocab.note: 多益常見於報告與新聞，修飾 increase、drop、change 等動詞，表示變化很大且很突然，常帶有「幅度驚人」的語氣。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: drastically 修飾動詞或形容詞，位置在動詞前後都可以（drastically reduce / fell drastically），前面不加 very。

example.en: Our sales dropped drastically after the main store closed.
example.zh: 主要門市關閉後，我們的銷售大幅下滑。

example.en: The market has changed drastically in the last two years.
example.zh: 這個市場在過去兩年劇烈改變。

example.en: We must drastically reduce our travel costs this year.
example.zh: 我們今年必須大幅降低差旅成本。

examples.en: Prices rose drastically because of the shortage of raw materials.
examples.zh: 由於原料短缺，價格大幅上漲。

examples.en: The new system drastically cut the time we spend on reports.
examples.zh: 新系統大幅縮短了我們做報告的時間。

examples.en: The two plans are drastically different in cost and schedule.
examples.zh: 這兩個計畫在成本與時程上差異極大。

similar.diff: dramatically 較中性，表示顯著的變化；drastically 更強調突然、激烈，有時帶有負面感。

example.en: Online orders have increased dramatically since the sale began.
example.zh: 促銷開始後，網路訂單大幅增加。

similar.diff: sharply 常用來描述數字快速上升或下降。

example.en: Oil prices fell sharply at the end of the week.
example.zh: 油價在週末大跌。

derived.link: drastic 是詞幹；drastic + -ally 變成副詞，像 automatic → automatically。

extra_vocab.en: as said or shown by someone or something
extra_vocab.note: 多益常見於報告、公告與新聞，用來引出資料或說法的來源，如 according to the report、according to the schedule；語氣正式、客觀。
extra_vocab.pattern: According to + 來源, + 句子
extra_vocab.grammar_note: according to 後面接名詞（資料或人物），不接子句；不能說 according to me，表達自己的意見要用 in my opinion。

examples.en: According to the report, sales rose by ten percent in May.
examples.zh: 根據報告，五月的銷售成長了百分之十。

examples.en: According to our manager, the deadline has been moved to Friday.
examples.zh: 根據我們經理的說法，截止日已改到星期五。

examples.en: According to the schedule, the train leaves at eight.
examples.zh: 根據時刻表，火車八點出發。

examples.en: According to the new rule, visitors must wear a badge.
examples.zh: 依照新規定，訪客必須配戴識別證。

similar.diff: based on 表示「以…為依據」來做決定或計算，後面接的是依據的內容。

example.en: Prices are based on the size of the order.
example.zh: 價格是依訂單的大小決定的。

similar.diff: 指文件裡「明文寫著」，常見於合約與公告。

example.en: As stated in the contract, either side may end the deal.
example.zh: 如合約所載，任何一方都可以終止合作。

confusable.diff: accordingly 是副詞，意思是「相應地、依情況」，不接名詞當來源。

example.en: We received your request and will act accordingly.
example.zh: 我們已收到您的要求，會依此處理。

extra_vocab.zh: 持續不斷的；固定不變的
extra_vocab.en: happening all the time, or not changing
extra_vocab.note: 多益常見於 constant demand、constant change、constant temperature，強調「一直發生、沒有間斷」或「保持不變」，語氣中性。

example.en: There is a constant demand for skilled engineers in this city.
example.zh: 這個城市對有技術的工程師一直有需求。

example.en: The tech industry is in a state of constant change.
example.zh: 科技業處於不斷變動的狀態。

example.en: A constant supply of water is essential for the factory.
example.zh: 穩定的水源供應對工廠來說非常重要。

examples.en: Our team faces constant pressure to meet tight deadlines.
examples.zh: 我們的團隊持續面臨趕上緊迫截止日的壓力。

examples.en: The constant noise from the street made the call difficult.
examples.zh: 街上不斷的噪音讓通話變得困難。

examples.en: The constant delays are hurting our customer reviews.
examples.zh: 不斷的延誤正在傷害我們的顧客評價。

confusable.diff: consistent 是「前後一致、表現穩定」；constant 強調「一直持續、沒有間斷」。

example.en: Our sales team has delivered consistent results every quarter.
example.zh: 我們的業務團隊每一季都有穩定的成績。

similar.diff: continuous 強調中間完全沒有停止，常用於機器、流程。

example.en: The machine needs continuous power to run all night.
example.zh: 這台機器需要持續供電才能整夜運轉。

similar.diff: steady 強調穩定、平穩地進行，常用於成長或收入。

example.en: Sales showed a steady increase over the last year.
example.zh: 過去一年銷售呈現穩定的成長。

derived.link: constant + -ly，形容詞變副詞，像 quick → quickly。

senses.en: happening again and again without stopping

example.en: We receive constant calls from customers about the new app.
example.zh: 我們不斷接到顧客詢問新應用程式的電話。

senses.distinguish: 和 temperature、speed、level 等名詞搭配時，指「穩定不變」。

example.en: Keep the storage room at a constant temperature all year.
example.zh: 請讓儲藏室全年保持固定的溫度。

extra_vocab.en: money given to make up for a loss, or money paid for work
extra_vocab.note: 多益常見於客服、保險與人資：補償損失或不便時，用 compensation for + 損失的原因；談薪資與福利時，compensation package 指整體薪酬。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: compensation 是不可數名詞，不加 s；補償的原因用 for（compensation for the delay），給誰則說 give someone compensation。

example.en: She asked for compensation for the damaged package.
example.zh: 她要求賠償那個受損的包裹。

example.en: Passengers receive compensation when their flights are canceled.
example.zh: 航班被取消時，乘客可獲得賠償。

example.en: The compensation package includes a bonus and health insurance.
example.zh: 這份薪酬待遇包含獎金與健康保險。

example.en: You can claim compensation within thirty days of the accident.
example.zh: 事故發生後三十天內，您可以請求賠償。

examples.en: We offer full compensation for any late delivery.
examples.zh: 任何延遲送達我們都提供完整賠償。

examples.en: Her compensation depends on her sales and years of service.
examples.zh: 她的薪酬取決於她的業績與年資。

examples.en: The company paid compensation to workers hurt on the job.
examples.zh: 公司賠償了在工作中受傷的員工。

confusable.diff: complement 是「補充、搭配」，拼法與 compliment（稱讚）、compensation 都容易搞混。
confusable.usage: complement 是及物動詞，後面接受詞：complement our system；compensation 是不可數名詞，後面接 for。

example.en: The new software will complement our existing system.
example.zh: 新軟體將和我們現有的系統相輔相成。

similar.diff: reimbursement 是把你先墊的錢還給你；compensation 是補償損失、不便或給付酬勞。

example.en: Please submit receipts to get reimbursement for travel costs.
example.zh: 請提交收據以取得差旅費用的報銷。

example.en: Her salary is paid on the twenty-fifth of every month.
example.zh: 她的薪水在每個月二十五日發放。

example.en: Health insurance is one of the main benefits of this job.
example.zh: 健康保險是這份工作的主要福利之一。

derived.link: compensate 是詞幹；去掉 e 加 -ion 變成名詞，像 create → creation。

senses.en: money paid to make up for a loss or problem

example.en: The airline gave us compensation for the long delay.
example.zh: 航空公司因為長時間的延誤而給了我們賠償。

senses.en: all the money and benefits paid for a job
senses.distinguish: 談 job、executive、package 時，指薪水加獎金、福利的整體報酬，而不是賠償。

example.en: Total compensation for this job includes salary, bonuses, and insurance.
example.zh: 這份工作的總薪酬包括薪水、獎金與保險。
